title: Coverage and disjointness of representative components
statement: Let R and H be commutative rings, g in R, and ι:R→H. Let C be a domain H-algebra finite and faithfully flat over H. A finite group G acts on C by H-algebra maps ρ, preserving identity and multiplication. Assume h=algebraMap H C (ι(g)) is nonzero, D(h)→Spec H is etale, and any two field-valued points of C over H on which h is nonzero differ by a unique ρ(ζ). Let p:Y→Spec R factor through a finite etale j:Y→D(g). Given t:T→Spec R, k:D(h)→T over Spec R, and a splitting δ:Y×T≅∐(Fin d) T over T, use the explicit label action A of [lem-sbc-affine-torsor-split-label-laws]. Let r:Fin m→Fin d be complete and distinct orbit representatives and K_i their exact stabilizers. Put F_i=⋂ζ∈K_i Eq(ρ(ζ),id), U_i=D(algebraMap H F_i (ι(g))), and q_i:D(h)→U_i the restriction of Spec(F_i→C). Suppose open immersions f_i:U_i→Y×Spec H are given over Spec H and q_i followed by f_i and projection to Y equals the r(i)-th split section pulled back along k. Then the opensRange of the f_i have supremum top and are pairwise disjoint.

source.place: Tag 03SF, finite Galois covers and permutation sets; stabilizer quotient argument

proof.text: Apply the point-lifting theorem to any point z of Y×Spec H, obtaining z=s_y(a). Completeness chooses i,ζ with A(ζ)(r_i)=y. The single-component orbit-image criterion gives z∈opensRange f_i, hence the supremum is top.

If z belongs to both component images, lift it as s_y(a). The image criterion gives α,β with A(α)(r_i)=y=A(β)(r_j). The homomorphism laws imply A(β⁻¹α)(r_i)=r_j. Distinctness forces i=j, proving pairwise disjointness.

proof_origin.note: Point lifting proved from Mathlib; coverage and disjointness reduced to the strictly single-component orbit-image criterion.
